key_insight: An exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion model shows that CT-CS energy alignment is the main lever controlling the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaic devices.
engineering_relevance: The model gives device engineers a practical way to tune singlet/triplet energetics and triplet recycling to improve photocurrent while limiting efficiency losses.
method: Couples singlet and triplet exciton kinetics to drift-diffusion charge transport in a self-consistent EKDD framework.
Solves reversible photophysical transitions and state populations for transient and steady-state device response.
Sweeps LE-CT, CT-CS, LE-T offsets and triplet-transfer rates to map charge generation, recombination, and voltage loss.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends.
watch_item: Design rules depend strongly on accurate CT-CS and triplet-transfer parameters, so performance predictions may be sensitive to material-specific energetics and temperature.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
